title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: share agents with a Microsoft Teams team
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and documented governance controls are supported. It appropriately distinguishes the organisation-wide sharing control from the Teams-team option, for which a dedicated control was not found.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team.
claims.quote: With this feature, users will be able to share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team.

claims.claim: Users can search for and select teams in the agent sharing dialog.
claims.quote: Users can search for and find teams in the agent sharing dialog box.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users can choose to send a notification to the selected team's main channel.
claims.quote: Users can also send a notification to the main channel of that team to make members aware of an agent being shared with them

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The notification informs team members about the shared agent and provides an installation link.
claims.quote: When sharing, users can send a notification to the team's main channel to inform members and provide an easy installation link.

claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is March CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "March CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-04-10T21:45:06.
The release notes list Share agents to Teams under Copilot extensibility for updates between April 7 and April 21, 2026.
claims.quote:
April 21, 2026
Updates released between April 7, 2026, April 21, 2026
Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility
Share agents to Teams

claims.claim: The July 01, 2026 release-note entry lists the same feature under Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio.
claims.quote:
July 01, 2026
Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio
Share agents to Teams
Roadmap ID: 557947

claims.claim: The July release-note instructions begin by telling users to open the agent sharing dialog in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Open the agent sharing dialog in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The Agent Builder sharing dialog accepts a name, group or email.
claims.quote: In the share dialog, enter a name, group, or email in the Add a name, group, or email box.

claims.claim: Agent Builder offers a Can edit role for owners.
claims.quote: Choose Can edit to add them as an owner with full edit and management rights.

claims.claim: Agent Builder offers a Can chat role for chat users.
claims.quote: Choose Can chat to add them as a chat user who can only interact with the agent.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio new agent experience supports sharing with individual users.
claims.quote:
For each agent, you can share with:
Individual users by using their email or user name

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio new agent experience supports sharing with specified security groups.
claims.quote: All members within security groups that you specify

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio new agent experience supports sharing with the whole organisation.
claims.quote: Your entire organization

claims.claim: Neither of the two cited sharing pages describes the roadmap's Teams-team option.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams team" "agent" "sharing" "Can chat"; read plugins/agent-builder-share-manage-agents and microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent. Neither describes selecting a Teams team and notifying its main channel.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: users choose a team and whether to notify it rather than an agent being shared automatically.
claims.quote: Users can now share an agent with a Microsoft Teams team by selecting a team in the sharing dialog. Users can also notify the team's main channel so team members are aware of the agent and can install it.

claims.where: controls[2]; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI or API switch is documented for Teams-team sharing or its main-channel notification.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "agent sharing" "admin" "notification" Copilot sharing switch; "Teams" "sharing" "agent" "Graph" "sharing policy"; "Copilot" "share agents" "Teams team" "PowerShell". Read agent-settings, utcm-agent-resources, both sharing pages and release notes; no dedicated switch found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state that the org-wide Sharing setting controls the Teams-team option.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "sharing" "agent" "Graph" "sharing policy" and "557947" "control" "sharing". Read agent-settings, Agent Builder sharing and utcm-agent-resources: the setting covers sharing with everyone in the organisation, not an expressly identified Teams-team option.

claims.claim: Sharing with a team makes the agent accessible to that team's members.
claims.quote: This feature allows users to share their agent directly with a Microsoft Teams team, making it easier for teams to discover, install, and start using agents together.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent access and knowledge-source access are distinct; sharing the agent alone does not grant access to all its source content.
claims.quote:
Access to an agent and access to its knowledge sources are distinct:
SharePoint and OneDrive sources: Existing file permissions and sensitivity labels apply. Sharing the agent alone doesn't grant access to all its source content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Existing file permissions and sensitivity labels apply to SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge sources.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive sources: Existing file permissions and sensitivity labels apply.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Files uploaded from a device become embedded knowledge.
claims.quote: Uploaded files: Files uploaded from a device become embedded knowledge.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Anyone with agent access can receive responses grounded in uploaded content, subject to that content's sensitivity-label permissions.
claims.quote: Anyone who can access the agent can receive responses grounded in that content, subject to the embedded content's sensitivity-label permissions.

claims.claim: A team's main channel is a shared conversation space rather than an individually addressed recipient list.
claims.quote: Every team in Teams has a "General" channel. General channels are standard channels that permanently appear at the top of the channel list of a team. The General channel can be used as a space for announcements or conversation

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: A group added to an Agent Builder agent can only be a Can chat user, not an owner.
claims.quote: You can't add a group as an owner. When you add a group, it can only be a chat user (Can chat). To grant owner rights, add individual users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited documentation does not explicitly identify the role granted through this Teams-team option.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams team" "agent" "sharing" "Can chat". Read both sharing pages and the release notes: group chat permissions are described for Agent Builder, but the Teams-team feature's entries do not name a role.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Agent Builder sharing page says recipients need the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence type required by the agent's capabilities.
claims.quote: Users can only add agents that are shared with them when they have the type of Microsoft 365 Copilot license required for accessing the capabilities configured in that agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Attempts to use an agent without the appropriate capability licence might result in an error.
claims.quote: If a user doesn't have the appropriate license for an agent's capabilities, attempts to use the agent might result in an error.

claims.claim: The roadmap description describes sharing, discovery and notification, not new agent actions.
claims.quote: Users can search for and find teams in the agent sharing dialog box. Users can also send a notification to the main channel of that team

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changes to the Sharing setting apply only to new sharing actions.
claims.quote: Changes to the sharing setting apply only to new sharing actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Existing shared-agent access remains until the agent's sharing settings are manually updated.
claims.quote: Existing shared agents remain accessible unless you manually update their sharing settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence for this feature.
claims.quote: With this feature, users will be able to share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page describes Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat as available to all Microsoft 365 users.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is a broadly accessible AI chat interface that is available to all Microsoft 365 users.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: In the pay-as-you-go model, consumption is measured in Copilot Credits and usage billing applies to tenant-data-grounded agents.
claims.quote: Belong to tenants with pay-as-you-go billing enabled (consumed as Copilot Credits). Users can access Copilot Chat and agents without a full Copilot license. Usage billing applies to agents grounded in tenant data

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate price, meter or licensing rule specific to sharing an agent with a Teams team is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "share agents" "Teams" "price" billing. Read plugins/prerequisites, plugins/cost-considerations, Agent Builder licensing, both sharing pages and release notes; found capability-based licensing and usage billing but no separate Teams-team sharing price, meter or entitlement.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects licence-based and usage-based access according to agent capabilities.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license - Users with a Microsoft 365 subscription and a Copilot add-on license have full access to Copilot agent experiences across supported apps and platforms.
Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go)

claims.claim: The prerequisites page allows pay-as-you-go users to access agents without a full Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Users can access Copilot Chat and agents without a full Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio new-experience sharing page separately requires recipients to have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license. Users who don't have a license can sign up for a trial.

claims.claim: The org-wide Sharing setting defaults to All users.
claims.quote: All users (default): Everyone can share agents with the organization.

claims.claim: No users disables org-wide sharing while allowing sharing directly with specific individuals.
claims.quote: No users - Disable sharing at the org level, but users can still share directly with specific individuals.

claims.claim: The Sharing control applies only to agents built with Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Sharing control only applies to agents built with Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for applying the documented Agent resources through TCM.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Sharing controls who can share Agent Builder agents with the organisation.
claims.quote: Org-wide sharing: In Agents > Settings > Sharing, control who can share agents built in Agent Builder with the organization.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors applies the sharing resource when mode is applyOnce.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls which users or groups can access and install agents and plugins.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.
Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors applies the useraccess resource when mode is applyOnce.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The Tenant Configuration Management Agent resources and the Graph beta API are preview functionality.
claims.quote: This article lists the Agent resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: The mode property can be set to applyOnce to apply the desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.

claims.claim: The resourceType value microsoft.agent.sharing configures organisation-wide Agent Builder sharing.
claims.quote:
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.sharing"
organizationWideSharingAssignment | Write | UserAssignment | Configures which users can share agents with everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: The resourceType value microsoft.agent.useraccess configures general agent and plugin access.
claims.quote:
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.useraccess"
valueObject | Write | AgentUserAccessValueObject | Configures who can access agents and plugins.

claims.claim: The sharing resource's userAssignmentCategory supports everyone and noOne.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can share agents with everyone in the organization. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: The useraccess resource's userAssignmentCategory supports everyone and noOne.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: Applying these Agent resources requires the TCM service principal to have the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: The admin-centre Sharing control offers All users, No users and Specific users.
claims.quote:
All users - All users can share their agents with others in your tenant.
No users - Disable sharing at the org level, but users can still share directly with specific individuals.
Specific users - Restrict broad sharing permissions to designated groups.

claims.claim: The Agent Builder overview limits automatic SharePoint file and folder sharing to specific security groups, not everyone in the organisation.
claims.quote: Auto sharing SharePoint files and folders is only supported when sharing with specific security groups and not everyone in the organization.
